notes.summary: ECDSA signatures in `@dream/bytes`: ES256 and ES384 tokens from the P-256 and P-384 keys API consoles hand out, SEC1 or PKCS#8, PEM or DER.
added: `bytes.ecdsaSign(data, privateKey, algorithm)`, behind `bytes-crypto`: the raw ECDSA signature of `data`, `r` then `s`, each fixed-width and big-endian, the form JSON Web Tokens carry. `sha256` signs under a P-256 key (ES256, 64 bytes), `sha384` under a P-384 key (ES384, 96 bytes). The key is PKCS#8 (`BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`) or SEC1 (`BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY`, what OpenSSL writes and most consoles issue), PEM or DER, with its public point. ECDSA is randomized, so every call signs afresh and every signature verifies.
notes.migration:
Nothing to change. Take 2.6.0 in place of 2.5.0.

Check an ECDSA signature by verifying it, never by comparing its bytes with another: two signatures of the same data by the same key differ. A key on the other curve, an RSA key, or anything else is refused with a message that never quotes the key, as `rsaSign` refuses one.
